baal-gad_140.name: Baal-gad
baal-gad_140.what: A town in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon, marking the northern limit of Joshua's conquest.
baal-gad_140.today: Exact site unknown; likely in southern Lebanon near the foot of Mount Hermon.
key: Joshua's conquest reached from Mount Halak in the south to Baal-gad in the north (Joshua 11).
Baal-gad is named again as the northern edge of the land Joshua took (Joshua 12).
God lists the region from Baal-gad toward Lebanon as land still to be possessed (Joshua 13).

baal-meon_144.name: Baal-meon
baal-meon_144.what: A town east of the Dead Sea, settled by Reuben and later held by Moab.
baal-meon_144.today: Likely modern Ma'in, southwest of Madaba in Jordan.
key: The Reubenites rebuilt Baal-meon and gave it a new name (Numbers 32).
Reubenite clans lived in the area from Aroer to Nebo and Baal-meon (1 Chronicles 5).
Ezekiel names Baal-meon among Moab's prized cities that God would open to invaders (Ezekiel 25).

baal-peor_145.name: Baal-peor
baal-peor_145.what: A site in Moab where Israel worshiped the local god Baal and fell into sexual immorality.
baal-peor_145.today: Exact site unknown; in the plains of Moab near Mount Nebo, Jordan.
key: Moses reminds Israel that the LORD destroyed everyone who followed the Baal of Peor (Deuteronomy 4).
The psalmist recalls how Israel joined the Baal of Peor and provoked God's anger (Psalms 106).
Hosea points back to Baal-peor as the place Israel first devoted itself to shameful idolatry (Hosea 9).

baal-zephon_149.name: Baal-zephon
baal-zephon_149.what: A landmark in Egypt near the sea, where Israel camped just before crossing the Red Sea.
baal-zephon_149.today: Exact site unknown; in northeastern Egypt near the Red Sea crossing.
key: God told Israel to camp facing Baal-zephon, and Pharaoh's army overtook them there by the sea (Exodus 14).
Baal-zephon is listed on Moses' record of Israel's journey out of Egypt (Numbers 33).

baalah_135.name: Baalah
baalah_135.what: Another name for Kiriath-jearim, a town on Judah's northern border where the ark rested for years.
baalah_135.today: Kiriath-jearim, likely at Deir el-Azar near Abu Ghosh, west of Jerusalem.
key: Baalah, identified as Kiriath-jearim, marks part of Judah's northern boundary (Joshua 15).
David and all Israel went to Baalah to bring the ark of God up from there (1 Chronicles 13).

besor_181.name: Besor
besor_181.what: A brook in southwestern Judah that David's men crossed while pursuing the Amalekite raiders.
besor_181.today: Likely Nahal Besor (Wadi Ghazzeh), flowing toward the coast near Gaza.
key: Two hundred of David's men were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor and stayed behind (1 Samuel 30).
After the victory, David ruled that those who stayed by the baggage would share equally in the spoil (1 Samuel 30).

beth-arabah_188.name: Beth-arabah
beth-arabah_188.what: A town in the Jordan Valley on the border between Judah and Benjamin.
beth-arabah_188.today: Exact site uncertain; likely near the Jordan River southeast of Jericho.
key: Beth-arabah lies on Judah's northern boundary and is listed among Judah's wilderness towns (Joshua 15).
Beth-arabah also appears among the towns allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (Joshua 18).

beth-hoglah_213.name: Beth-hoglah
beth-hoglah_213.what: A border town near the Jordan River between the territories of Judah and Benjamin.
beth-hoglah_213.today: Likely near Ein Hajla, southeast of Jericho.
key: Judah's northern boundary went up to Beth-hoglah from the mouth of the Jordan (Joshua 15).
Beth-hoglah is named on Benjamin's border and among Benjamin's towns (Joshua 18).

beth-shan_232.name: Beth-shan
beth-shan_232.what: A fortified city at the junction of the Jezreel and Jordan valleys.
beth-shan_232.today: Tel Beit She'an, beside the modern town of Beit She'an, Israel.
key: The Philistines fastened the bodies of Saul and his sons to the wall of Beth-shan (1 Samuel 31).
Men of Jabesh-gilead traveled by night to take the bodies down and bury them (1 Samuel 31).
David later recovered the bones of Saul and Jonathan, taken from Beth-shan's square (2 Samuel 21).

beth-zur_242.name: Beth-zur
beth-zur_242.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, north of Hebron, guarding the southern approach to Jerusalem.
beth-zur_242.today: Khirbet et-Tubeiqah, about four miles north of Hebron.
key: Beth-zur is listed among the towns of Judah's hill country (Joshua 15).
King Rehoboam fortified Beth-zur as one of Judah's defensive cities (2 Chronicles 11).
A ruler of half the district of Beth-zur helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).

bethphage_229.name: Bethphage
bethphage_229.what: A village on the Mount of Olives near Bethany, just east of Jerusalem.
bethphage_229.today: Likely on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives, near modern et-Tur.
key: Near Bethphage, Jesus sent two disciples to bring a donkey and her colt (Matthew 21).
Mark records Jesus nearing Bethphage and Bethany before entering Jerusalem (Mark 11).
From near Bethphage Jesus began his royal entry as disciples praised God (Luke 19).

caphtor_275.name: Caphtor
caphtor_275.what: The coastland from which the Philistines originally came, across the Mediterranean.
key: The Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor, destroyed the Avvim and settled in their place (Deuteronomy 2).
Jeremiah calls the Philistines the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor (Jeremiah 47).
God says he brought the Philistines from Caphtor, as he brought Israel from Egypt (Amos 9).

carchemish_277.name: Carchemish
carchemish_277.what: A major city on the upper Euphrates, site of a decisive battle between Egypt and Babylon.
carchemish_277.today: Ruins at Karkamis on the Turkey–Syria border, near Jarabulus.
key: King Josiah was killed opposing Pharaoh Neco on his way to fight at Carchemish (2 Chronicles 35).
Assyria boasts that conquered cities, including Carchemish, show its power is unstoppable (Isaiah 10).
Nebuchadnezzar defeated Neco's army at Carchemish by the Euphrates (Jeremiah 46).

daberath_319.name: Daberath
daberath_319.what: A town near Mount Tabor on the border of Zebulun, later given to the Levites.
daberath_319.today: Likely Daburiyya, at the western foot of Mount Tabor, Israel.
key: Daberath is named on the boundary of Zebulun's territory (Joshua 19).
Daberath was given from Issachar's land to the Gershonite Levites (Joshua 21).
The Chronicler lists Daberath again among the Levites' towns (1 Chronicles 6).

decapolis_328.name: Decapolis
decapolis_328.what: A region of ten Greek-influenced cities, mostly east and southeast of the Sea of Galilee.
decapolis_328.today: Parts of northern Jordan, southern Syria, and northern Israel.
key: Great crowds from the Decapolis followed Jesus early in his ministry (Matthew 4).
The man freed from many demons proclaimed in the Decapolis what Jesus had done (Mark 5).
Jesus passed through the Decapolis region and healed a deaf man with a speech impediment (Mark 7).

ebenezer_350.name: Ebenezer
ebenezer_350.what: A place near Aphek where Israel lost the ark to the Philistines, and later a memorial stone.
ebenezer_350.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Izbet Sartah, near Aphek east of Tel Aviv.
key: Israel camped at Ebenezer and was defeated by the Philistines, who captured the ark (1 Samuel 4).
The Philistines carried the ark from Ebenezer to Ashdod (1 Samuel 5).
After victory, Samuel set up a stone named Ebenezer, saying the LORD had helped them (1 Samuel 7).

elath_366.name: Elath
elath_366.what: A port town at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, contested between Judah and Edom.
elath_366.today: Near modern Eilat, Israel, and Aqaba, Jordan.
key: Israel passed by Elath and Ezion-geber on its way around Edom (Deuteronomy 2).
King Azariah rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah (2 Kings 14).
In Ahaz's day Rezin recovered Elath for Edom and drove out the people of Judah (2 Kings 16).

eloth_375.name: Eloth
eloth_375.what: Another spelling of Elath, a port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber.
eloth_375.today: Near modern Eilat, Israel, and Aqaba, Jordan.
key: Solomon built a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber near Eloth on the Red Sea (1 Kings 9).
The Chronicler repeats that Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth by the sea (2 Chronicles 8).
King Uzziah rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah (2 Chronicles 26).

en-dor_385.name: En-dor
en-dor_385.what: A town south of Mount Tabor, best known as the home of the medium Saul consulted.
en-dor_385.today: Likely near the village of Indur, south of Mount Tabor, Israel.
key: En-dor was assigned to Manasseh, though it lay within Issachar and Asher (Joshua 17).
On the eve of battle, a disguised Saul consulted a medium at En-dor (1 Samuel 28).
The psalmist recalls Sisera and Jabin, who perished at En-dor (Psalms 83).

ephrath_403.name: Ephrath
ephrath_403.what: An older name for Bethlehem in Judah, near where Rachel died and was buried.
key: Rachel died giving birth to Benjamin on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem (Genesis 35).
Jacob tells Joseph he buried Rachel on the way to Ephrath (Genesis 48).

esau_408.name: Esau
esau_408.what: The land of Esau's descendants, Edom, sometimes called simply Esau or Mount Esau.
esau_408.today: Southern Jordan, south and east of the Dead Sea.
key: Esau, also called Edom, settled with his descendants in the hill country of Seir (Genesis 36).
Jeremiah announces that God will bring calamity on Esau and strip him bare (Jeremiah 49).
Obadiah foretells judgment on Mount Esau for its violence against Judah (Obadiah 1).

eshtemoa_412.name: Eshtemoa
eshtemoa_412.what: A town in the hill country of Judah south of Hebron, given to the priests.
key: Eshtemoa was given to the descendants of Aaron the priest (Joshua 21).
David sent some of the Amalekite spoil to the elders of Eshtemoa (1 Samuel 30).
Eshtemoa appears again among the priests' towns (1 Chronicles 6).

ezem_422.name: Ezem
ezem_422.what: A town in the Negev of southern Judah, later counted among Simeon's towns.
ezem_422.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev of southern Israel.
key: Ezem is listed among Judah's southernmost towns in the Negev (Joshua 15).
Ezem was included in the inheritance of Simeon within Judah's territory (Joshua 19).
The Chronicler names Ezem among the towns where Simeon's clans lived (1 Chronicles 4).

field_1229.name: Washer's Field
field_1229.what: A field outside Jerusalem's walls by the conduit of the upper pool, where cloth was washed.
field_1229.today: Exact site unknown; just outside ancient Jerusalem's walls.
key: Assyria's officials stood by the Washer's Field to demand Jerusalem's surrender (2 Kings 18).
Isaiah met King Ahaz by the conduit on the highway to the Washer's Field (Isaiah 7).
Isaiah records the Rabshakeh's arrival at the same spot during Hezekiah's reign (Isaiah 36).

fish_gate_426.name: Fish Gate
fish_gate_426.what: A gate in Jerusalem's northern wall, probably named for the fish market nearby.
fish_gate_426.today: Exact site unknown; on the north side of ancient Jerusalem.
key: Manasseh built an outer wall for Jerusalem around to the Fish Gate (2 Chronicles 33).
The sons of Hassenaah rebuilt the Fish Gate with its beams, doors, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
Zephaniah warns that a cry will rise from the Fish Gate on the day of the LORD (Zephaniah 1).

gate_of_the_fountain_428.name: Fountain Gate
gate_of_the_fountain_428.what: A gate at the southeast corner of Jerusalem's wall, near the Pool of Siloam.
gate_of_the_fountain_428.today: Exact site unknown; near the southern end of the City of David, Jerusalem.
key: During his night inspection, Nehemiah reached the Fountain Gate but could not pass through (Nehemiah 2).
Shallun rebuilt the Fountain Gate and the wall of the Pool of Shelah (Nehemiah 3).
At the wall's dedication, a procession went up by the Fountain Gate to the City of David (Nehemiah 12).

gath-rimmon_444.name: Gath-rimmon
gath-rimmon_444.what: A town on the coastal plain allotted to Dan and given to the Levites.
gath-rimmon_444.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly Tell Jerisheh near Tel Aviv.
key: Gath-rimmon is listed in the inheritance of the tribe of Dan (Joshua 19).
Gath-rimmon was given from Dan's land to the Kohathite Levites (Joshua 21).
The Chronicler lists Gath-rimmon among the Levites' towns (1 Chronicles 6).

gebal_449.name: Gebal
gebal_449.what: An ancient Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast, north of Sidon.
gebal_449.today: Byblos (Jbeil), on the coast of Lebanon north of Beirut.
key: Men of Gebal helped prepare timber and stone for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5).
Gebal is named among the nations conspiring against God's people (Psalms 83).
Gebal's skilled elders repaired the seams of Tyre's ships (Ezekiel 27).

gederah_452.name: Gederah
gederah_452.what: A town in the lowland (Shephelah) of Judah.
gederah_452.today: Exact site uncertain; in the Shephelah of Judah.
key: Gederah is listed among the towns of Judah's lowland (Joshua 15).
Potters who worked for the king lived at Netaim and Gederah (1 Chronicles 4).
Jozabad of Gederah joined David's mighty men at Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12).

gennesaret_458.name: Gennesaret
gennesaret_458.what: A fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, which also lent the lake its name.
gennesaret_458.today: The plain of Ginosar, on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, Israel.
key: After crossing the lake, Jesus landed at Gennesaret, and all who touched his garment were healed (Matthew 14).
Mark records people bringing the sick on mats as soon as Jesus reached Gennesaret (Mark 6).
By the lake of Gennesaret, Jesus taught from Peter's boat and called him after a great catch (Luke 5).

gilboa_474.name: Gilboa
gilboa_474.what: A mountain ridge at the southeastern edge of the Jezreel Valley, where Saul died.
gilboa_474.today: Mount Gilboa, in northern Israel near Beit She'an.
key: Saul gathered Israel at Gilboa, facing the Philistine army camped at Shunem (1 Samuel 28).
In his lament, David asked that no dew or rain fall on Gilboa (2 Samuel 1).
The Philistines had killed Saul on Gilboa, and David later reburied his bones (2 Samuel 21).

golgotha_487.name: Golgotha
golgotha_487.what: The place just outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified, meaning Place of a Skull.
golgotha_487.today: Traditionally at the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, Jerusalem.
key: Soldiers brought Jesus to Golgotha and offered him wine mixed with gall (Matthew 27).
Mark explains that Golgotha means Place of a Skull, where Jesus was crucified (Mark 15).
Jesus carried his own cross to Golgotha, where he was crucified between two others (John 19).

goshen_491.name: Goshen
goshen_491.what: A district and town in the southern hill country of Judah, distinct from Goshen in Egypt.
goshen_491.today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country south of Hebron.
key: Joshua struck the land from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza and all the country of Goshen (Joshua 10).
Goshen is listed among the regions Joshua took in the south (Joshua 11).
A town named Goshen appears among Judah's hill-country towns (Joshua 15).

habor_499.name: Habor
habor_499.what: A river in upper Mesopotamia, the river of Gozan, where Assyria resettled exiled Israelites.
habor_499.today: The Khabur River in northeastern Syria.
key: After Samaria fell, the king of Assyria placed Israelites by the Habor, the river of Gozan (2 Kings 17).
The account of Israel's exile to the Habor is repeated in Hezekiah's reign (2 Kings 18).
Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh were exiled to Habor and nearby places (1 Chronicles 5).

hachilah_500.name: Hachilah
hachilah_500.what: A hill in the wilderness near Ziph where David hid from Saul.
hachilah_500.today: Exact site unknown; in the Judean wilderness southeast of Hebron.
key: The Ziphites told Saul that David was hiding on the hill of Hachilah (1 Samuel 23).
Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, and David spared his life while he slept (1 Samuel 26).

hadid_503.name: Hadid
hadid_503.what: A town near Lod in the lowlands, resettled by returning exiles.
key: People of Lod, Hadid, and Ono were among those returning from Babylon (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's list repeats the returnees from Lod, Hadid, and Ono (Nehemiah 7).
Members of the tribe of Benjamin settled in Hadid (Nehemiah 11).

halah_508.name: Halah
halah_508.what: A district in Assyria where the king resettled Israelites exiled from Samaria.
halah_508.today: Exact site uncertain; likely in northern Iraq, northeast of Nineveh.
key: The king of Assyria carried Israel away and placed them in Halah (2 Kings 17).
Halah is named again in the account of Samaria's fall during Hezekiah's reign (2 Kings 18).
Exiles from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh were taken to Halah (1 Chronicles 5).

harosheth-hagoyim_530.name: Harosheth-hagoyim
harosheth-hagoyim_530.what: The home base of Sisera, commander of the Canaanite king Jabin's army.
harosheth-hagoyim_530.today: Exact site uncertain; probably near the Kishon River in northern Israel.
key: Sisera, commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-hagoyim (Judges 4).
Barak pursued Sisera's chariots and army all the way to Harosheth-hagoyim (Judges 4).

hena_560.name: Hena
hena_560.what: A city conquered by Assyria, cited by Sennacherib's officials as proof that no god could resist them.
hena_560.today: Exact site unknown; possibly along the middle Euphrates.
key: The Rabshakeh asked where the gods of Hena were, to shake Jerusalem's trust in God (2 Kings 18).
Sennacherib's letter to Hezekiah again asked what became of the king of Hena (2 Kings 19).
Isaiah records the same boast about Hena, before God delivered Jerusalem (Isaiah 37).

ibleam_589.name: Ibleam
ibleam_589.what: A Canaanite town in the northern hill country, allotted to Manasseh.
ibleam_589.today: Khirbet Bel'ameh, just south of Jenin.
key: Ibleam was assigned to Manasseh, though it lay within Issachar and Asher (Joshua 17).
Manasseh failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Ibleam (Judges 1).
Jehu's men wounded King Ahaziah at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam (2 Kings 9).

ijon_594.name: Ijon
ijon_594.what: A town in the far north of Israel, repeatedly taken by invading armies.
ijon_594.today: Likely Tell ed-Dibbin, in the Marjayoun valley of southern Lebanon.
key: At King Asa's request, Ben-hadad of Syria conquered Ijon (1 Kings 15).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured Ijon and deported its people (2 Kings 15).
The Chronicler repeats Ben-hadad's attack on Ijon (2 Chronicles 16).

ivvah_605.name: Ivvah
ivvah_605.what: A city conquered by Assyria, cited by Sennacherib's officials as proof of their power.
ivvah_605.today: Exact site unknown; possibly in Syria or Mesopotamia.
key: The Rabshakeh asked where the gods of Ivvah were, to frighten Jerusalem (2 Kings 18).
Sennacherib's letter to Hezekiah again named the king of Ivvah (2 Kings 19).
Isaiah records the same boast about Ivvah, before God struck the Assyrian army (Isaiah 37).

jokneam_649.name: Jokneam
jokneam_649.what: A Canaanite town near Mount Carmel, later a Levitical city in Zebulun.
jokneam_649.today: Tel Yoqneam, at the northwestern edge of the Jezreel Valley, Israel.
key: The king of Jokneam in Carmel was among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Zebulun's border reached the brook east of Jokneam (Joshua 19).
Jokneam was given from Zebulun to the Merarite Levites (Joshua 21).

jotbathah_656.name: Jotbathah
jotbathah_656.what: A campsite of Israel in the wilderness, described as a land with brooks of water.
jotbathah_656.today: Exact site unknown; possibly near the Gulf of Aqaba.
key: Israel set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah (Numbers 33).
Moses recalls Jotbathah as a land with brooks of water (Deuteronomy 10).

kabzeel_660.name: Kabzeel
kabzeel_660.what: A town in the Negev of southern Judah, home of David's mighty man Benaiah.
kabzeel_660.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negev of southern Israel.
key: Kabzeel is listed among Judah's southernmost towns toward Edom (Joshua 15).
Benaiah of Kabzeel, one of David's mighty men, struck down two champions of Moab (2 Samuel 23).
The Chronicler repeats Benaiah's deeds and his hometown of Kabzeel (1 Chronicles 11).

lehi_726.name: Lehi
lehi_726.what: A place in Judah where Samson killed a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone.
lehi_726.today: Exact site unknown; in Judah near the Philistine border.
key: The Philistines camped at Lehi, and Samson killed a thousand men with a fresh jawbone (Judges 15).
When Samson grew thirsty, God split open a hollow at Lehi and water came out (Judges 15).

lo-debar_732.name: Lo-debar
lo-debar_732.what: A town in Gilead east of the Jordan, home of Machir son of Ammiel.
lo-debar_732.today: Exact site unknown; in Gilead in northern Jordan.
key: David found Mephibosheth living in Machir's house at Lo-debar and showed him kindness (2 Samuel 9).
Machir of Lo-debar brought food and supplies to David during Absalom's revolt (2 Samuel 17).

lydda_741.name: Lydda
lydda_741.what: A town on the coastal plain near Joppa, where Peter healed a paralyzed man.
lydda_741.today: Modern Lod, Israel, near Ben Gurion Airport.
key: At Lydda Peter healed Aeneas, bedridden eight years, and residents turned to the Lord (Acts 9).
Disciples from nearby Joppa sent to Lydda for Peter after Tabitha died (Acts 9).

magog_754.name: Magog
magog_754.what: A distant northern land, home of Gog, who leads the nations against God's people.
magog_754.today: Exact site unknown; a remote northern region, possibly in Asia Minor.
key: Ezekiel prophesies against Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal (Ezekiel 38).
God promises to send fire on Magog and make his holy name known (Ezekiel 39).
After the thousand years, Satan gathers Gog and Magog for a final battle (Revelation 20).

marah_765.name: Marah
marah_765.what: A place in the wilderness of Shur whose name means bitter, for its undrinkable water.
marah_765.today: Exact site unknown; possibly Ain Hawarah in western Sinai.
key: At Marah the water was bitter until the LORD showed Moses a log that made it sweet (Exodus 15).
Marah is listed as Israel's campsite after three days in the wilderness (Numbers 33).

meribah-kadesh_784.name: Meribah-kadesh
meribah-kadesh_784.what: The waters at Kadesh where Moses and Aaron failed to honor God before Israel.
meribah-kadesh_784.today: Likely near Kadesh-barnea, at Ain el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai.
key: God told Moses he would not enter the land because he broke faith at Meribah-kadesh (Deuteronomy 32).
In Ezekiel's vision, Meribah-kadesh marks the southern border of the restored land (Ezekiel 47).
The southern boundary of the tribal allotments again runs to Meribah-kadesh (Ezekiel 48).

miletus_801.name: Miletus
miletus_801.what: A port city on the western coast of Asia Minor, south of Ephesus.
miletus_801.today: Ruins near the village of Balat in western Turkey.
key: Paul sent for the Ephesian elders to meet him at Miletus and gave them a farewell charge (Acts 20).
Paul tells Timothy he left Trophimus ill at Miletus (2 Timothy 4).

mount_tabor_857.name: Mount Tabor
mount_tabor_857.what: A prominent rounded mountain at the northeastern edge of the Jezreel Valley.
mount_tabor_857.today: Mount Tabor, east of Nazareth in northern Israel.
key: Deborah told Barak to gather ten thousand men at Mount Tabor (Judges 4).
Barak went down from Mount Tabor and the LORD routed Sisera's army (Judges 4).

nebo_884.name: Nebo
nebo_884.what: A town in Judah whose people returned from exile, distinct from Mount Nebo in Moab.
nebo_884.today: Exact site uncertain; possibly modern Nuba, northwest of Hebron.
key: The men of Nebo are counted among the exiles returning from Babylon (Ezra 2).
Some descendants of Nebo had married foreign women and agreed to put them away (Ezra 10).
Nehemiah's list counts the men of the other Nebo among the returnees (Nehemiah 7).

olivet_907.name: Olivet
olivet_907.what: The Mount of Olives, a ridge east of Jerusalem across the Kidron Valley.
olivet_907.today: The Mount of Olives, east of the Old City of Jerusalem.
key: Jesus approached Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet and sent for a colt (Luke 19).
During his final week Jesus taught in the temple and lodged nightly on Olivet (Luke 21).
After Jesus ascended, the apostles returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet (Acts 1).

perga_936.name: Perga
perga_936.what: A city in Pamphylia on the southern coast of Asia Minor, visited on Paul's first journey.
perga_936.today: Ruins near Aksu, east of Antalya in southern Turkey.
key: At Perga, John Mark left Paul and Barnabas and returned to Jerusalem (Acts 13).
On their return, Paul and Barnabas spoke the word in Perga before sailing home (Acts 14).

phenicia_944.name: Phoenicia
phenicia_944.what: The coastal region north of Israel that included the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
phenicia_944.today: The coast of modern Lebanon and parts of northern Israel and Syria.
key: Believers scattered after Stephen's death traveled as far as Phoenicia, preaching to Jews (Acts 11).
Passing through Phoenicia, Paul and Barnabas reported the Gentiles' conversion, bringing great joy (Acts 15).
Paul boarded a ship crossing to Phoenicia on his way to Jerusalem (Acts 21).

phrygia_946.name: Phrygia
phrygia_946.what: A region in the interior of Asia Minor, west of Galatia.
key: Jews from Phrygia were among those who heard the apostles at Pentecost (Acts 2).
Paul and his companions went through Phrygia and Galatia, kept from preaching in Asia (Acts 16).
Paul traveled through Phrygia strengthening all the disciples (Acts 18).

pi-hahiroth_948.name: Pi-hahiroth
pi-hahiroth_948.what: A campsite in Egypt between Migdol and the sea, where Israel stopped before crossing.
pi-hahiroth_948.today: Exact site unknown; in northeastern Egypt near the Red Sea crossing.
key: God had Israel camp before Pi-hahiroth, where Pharaoh's army overtook them (Exodus 14).
From Pi-hahiroth Israel passed through the sea into the wilderness (Numbers 33).

pontus_956.name: Pontus
pontus_956.what: A region of northern Asia Minor along the southern shore of the Black Sea.
pontus_956.today: The Black Sea coast of northern Turkey.
key: Jews from Pontus were present in Jerusalem at Pentecost (Acts 2).
Paul met Aquila, a Jew native to Pontus, in Corinth (Acts 18).
Peter addressed his first letter to God's scattered people in Pontus and nearby regions (1 Peter 1).

put_962.name: Put
put_962.what: An African nation west of Egypt whose soldiers fought as Egypt's allies.
key: Men of Put carrying shields marched in Egypt's army against Babylon (Jeremiah 46).
Ezekiel foretells that Put will fall by the sword along with Egypt (Ezekiel 30).
Nahum names Put among the helpers of Thebes, which still fell (Nahum 3).

rahab_969.name: Rahab
rahab_969.what: A poetic name for Egypt, also used of a sea monster symbolizing forces God subdues.
rahab_969.today: Egypt, used as a poetic name.
key: God lists Rahab, meaning Egypt, among nations whose people will be counted in Zion (Psalms 87).
The psalmist praises God, who crushed Rahab and scattered his enemies (Psalms 89).
Isaiah recalls the LORD's arm that cut Rahab in pieces, recalling the exodus (Isaiah 51).

ramoth_983.name: Ramoth
ramoth_983.what: A city in Gilead east of the Jordan, assigned to Gad as a city of refuge.
ramoth_983.today: Likely Tell er-Rumeith, in northern Jordan near the Syrian border.
key: Moses set apart Ramoth in Gilead as a city of refuge for Gad (Deuteronomy 4).
Joshua confirmed Ramoth in Gilead among the cities of refuge (Joshua 20).
Ramoth in Gilead was given to the Merarite Levites from Gad's territory (Joshua 21).

rimmon_1003.name: Rimmon
rimmon_1003.what: A rocky stronghold in Benjamin where survivors of the tribe took refuge.
rimmon_1003.today: Likely near the village of Rammun, east of Bethel.
key: After the battle at Gibeah, six hundred Benjaminites fled to the rock of Rimmon (Judges 20).
Israel sent word of peace to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon (Judges 21).

sardis_1027.name: Sardis
sardis_1027.what: A wealthy city in western Asia Minor, home to one of the seven churches of Revelation.
sardis_1027.today: Ruins near Sart, east of Izmir in western Turkey.
key: Sardis is one of seven cities whose churches John is told to write to (Revelation 1).
Christ tells Sardis it has a reputation for being alive but is dead (Revelation 3).
A few in Sardis have not soiled their garments and will walk with Christ in white (Revelation 3).

sela_1044.name: Sela
sela_1044.what: A rocky stronghold in Edom; the name means rock.
sela_1044.today: Possibly Petra or nearby as-Sela in southern Jordan.
key: The border of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela upward (Judges 1).
Moab's refugees are told to send lambs to Zion from Sela (Isaiah 16).
Isaiah calls the inhabitants of Sela to sing for joy to the LORD (Isaiah 42).

shechem_1178.name: Tower of Shechem
shechem_1178.what: A fortified stronghold of Shechem, connected with the temple of El-berith.
shechem_1178.today: Likely at Tell Balata, on the eastern edge of Nablus.
key: The leaders of the Tower of Shechem took refuge in the stronghold of the house of El-berith (Judges 9).
Abimelech set the stronghold on fire, and about a thousand people of the Tower of Shechem died (Judges 9).

shunem_1089.name: Shunem
shunem_1089.what: A town in the Jezreel Valley in Issachar, home of the Shunammite woman Elisha helped.
shunem_1089.today: Modern Sulam, near Afula in northern Israel.
key: Shunem is listed among the towns of Issachar (Joshua 19).
The Philistines camped at Shunem before the battle in which Saul died (1 Samuel 28).
A woman of Shunem hosted Elisha, who later raised her son to life (2 Kings 4).

siloam_1096.name: Siloam
siloam_1096.what: An area and pool at the southern end of ancient Jerusalem, fed by the Gihon spring.
siloam_1096.today: Pool remains excavated in the City of David, south of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Jesus asked whether eighteen killed when the tower in Siloam fell were worse sinners (Luke 13).
Jesus sent a man born blind to wash in the pool of Siloam, and he came back seeing (John 9).

sirion_1101.name: Sirion
sirion_1101.what: The Sidonian name for Mount Hermon, the highest mountain on Israel's northern border.
sirion_1101.today: Mount Hermon, on the border of Lebanon, Syria, and the Golan Heights.
key: Moses notes that the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion (Deuteronomy 3).
The psalmist says the LORD's voice makes Sirion leap like a young wild ox (Psalms 29).
Jeremiah asks whether the snow ever leaves the crags of Sirion, contrasting Israel's unfaithfulness (Jeremiah 18).

syene_1120.name: Syene
syene_1120.what: A town at Egypt's southern frontier on the Nile, marking the far limit of Egypt.
key: Isaiah foresees God's people gathering from distant places, including the land of Syene (Isaiah 49).
God promises to make Egypt desolate from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 29).
Ezekiel says Egypt's helpers will fall by the sword from Migdol to Syene (Ezekiel 30).

tappuah_1136.name: Tappuah
tappuah_1136.what: A Canaanite town on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh.
tappuah_1136.today: Likely Sheikh Abu Zarad, south of Nablus.
key: The king of Tappuah was among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Ephraim's border went west from Tappuah to the brook Kanah (Joshua 16).
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town itself belonged to Ephraim (Joshua 17).

tema_1149.name: Tema
tema_1149.what: An oasis town in northern Arabia on major caravan routes, settled by descendants of Ishmael.
key: Job compares his friends to dry streams that disappoint the caravans of Tema (Job 6).
The inhabitants of Tema are told to bring water and bread to fugitives (Isaiah 21).
Tema is among the nations made to drink the cup of God's wrath (Jeremiah 25).

uz_1190.name: Uz
uz_1190.what: The land where Job lived, apparently east of Israel and associated with Edom.
uz_1190.today: Exact site unknown; likely east or southeast of the Dead Sea.
key: Job, a blameless man who feared God, lived in the land of Uz (Job 1).
The kings of the land of Uz are among those made to drink God's cup of wrath (Jeremiah 25).
Lamentations addresses Edom as dwelling in the land of Uz, warning that judgment will reach her (Lamentations 4).

vale_of_siddim_1218.name: Valley of Siddim
vale_of_siddim_1218.what: A valley by the Salt Sea where four kings defeated the five kings of the plain.
vale_of_siddim_1218.today: Likely near the southern end of the Dead Sea; exact site unknown.
key: The five kings, including those of Sodom and Gomorrah, joined forces in the Valley of Siddim (Genesis 14).
The valley was full of bitumen pits, and fleeing kings fell into them (Genesis 14).

valley_of_elah_1201.name: Valley of Elah
valley_of_elah_1201.what: A valley in the Shephelah of Judah where David fought Goliath.
valley_of_elah_1201.today: The Elah Valley, west of Bethlehem near Azekah, Israel.
key: Saul's army camped in the Valley of Elah facing the Philistines, and David killed Goliath (1 Samuel 17).
At Nob the priest gave David the sword of Goliath, killed in the Valley of Elah (1 Samuel 21).

valley_of_hinnom_1207.name: Valley of Hinnom
aka: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
valley_of_hinnom_1207.what: A valley along the south and west sides of Jerusalem, later notorious for idolatrous child sacrifice.
valley_of_hinnom_1207.today: Ge Hinnom, below the south and west walls of Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Judah's northern boundary ran through the Valley of Hinnom, south of the Jebusite city (Joshua 15).
Benjamin's southern boundary went down the Valley of Hinnom (Joshua 18).
After the exile, people of Judah settled from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom (Nehemiah 11).

valley_of_jezreel_1211.name: Valley of Jezreel
valley_of_jezreel_1211.what: A broad, fertile valley in northern Israel, a frequent battlefield and route for armies.
valley_of_jezreel_1211.today: The Jezreel Valley, in northern Israel between Galilee and Samaria.
key: Canaanites in the Valley of Jezreel had iron chariots, troubling the tribe of Joseph (Joshua 17).
Midianites and Amalekites crossed the Jordan and camped in the Valley of Jezreel against Gideon (Judges 6).
God says he will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel (Hosea 1).

zanoah_1239.name: Zanoah
zanoah_1239.what: A town in the lowland of Judah, resettled after the exile.
zanoah_1239.today: Likely Khirbet Zanu, near Beth-shemesh, Israel.
key: Zanoah is listed among Judah's towns, both in the lowland and the hill country (Joshua 15).
Hanun and the people of Zanoah repaired Jerusalem's Valley Gate (Nehemiah 3).
Returning exiles from Judah settled in Zanoah and its villages (Nehemiah 11).
